title: Rubric R: reference materials
scale: Each criterion is scored 0-3: 0 not met, 1 weak, 2 good, 3 exemplary.
select_rule: Select a material only if every gate scores at least 2 and the weighted mean is at least 2.0 out of 3. Keep the top 2-3 per outcome.

criteria.name: Matches the outcome
criteria.check: Does the material teach the outcome's content and its action verb (for example 'solve', 'model', 'explain')?

criteria.name: Bloom level matches
criteria.check: Is the thinking level of the material (remember, understand, apply, analyse, evaluate, create) the same as the outcome's?

criteria.name: Accurate
criteria.check: Is every fact, example and worked answer correct? Any mathematical error scores 0 or 1.

criteria.name: Uses known prerequisites
criteria.check: Does it rely only on the listed prerequisites, or review what else it needs?

criteria.name: Trusted source
criteria.check: Is the source a provincial Department of Education, a provincially authorised resource, peer-reviewed open educational resource, or a journal? Unknown blogs and anonymous sites score 0-1.

criteria.name: Canadian context
criteria.check: Does it use Canadian contexts, units, spelling or curriculum language?

criteria.name: Easy to turn into slides
criteria.check: Is it organised in short, clear steps or examples that can become slides and narration?

criteria.name: Surfaces misconceptions
criteria.check: Does it name, show or address common mistakes for this outcome?

criteria.name: Licence allows use
criteria.check: Does the stated licence allow use in lessons (Creative Commons, public domain, public government document, or a justified fair dealing note)?

criteria.name: Accessible
criteria.check: Is it readable for the learners: plain language, clear layout, text alternatives for images?
